metadata.title: Young People’s Views of Government, Peaceful Coexistence, and Diversity in Five Latin American Countries
metadata.venue: IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study (ICCS) 2016 Latin American Report

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This ICCS 2016 Latin American report is based on the IEA’s large-scale survey design with student questionnaire data collected in participating countries (Chile, Colombia, Dominican Republic, Mexico, and Peru) as part of the ICCS 2016 regional Latin American component. The excerpt provided does not specify whether analysts applied student/sampling weights or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) in the reported analyses, so the weighting variables and variance estimation approach cannot be confirmed from the text shown. For ICCS analyses using the IEA international database, analysts should use the IEA-provided sampling weights and replicate weights (when available) to account for the complex multistage sampling design and clustering at school/class levels. The excerpt also does not describe any PV generation or missing-data imputation strategy, so those details should be taken from the ICCS 2016 technical report and the ICCS user guide for the public-use database.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The provided text is a book/report front matter and foreword/executive framing that does not describe any student-level cognitive outcome modeled with plausible values (PV-based achievement scales). Instead, it describes the scope of ICCS 2016 and the regional questionnaire component measuring civic/citizenship-related perceptions and attitudes. Because the excerpt does not include the methodological section where PVs and missing-data handling would be specified, missing-data handling is treated as not reported for this extraction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The excerpt states that the Latin American regional student questionnaire was completed by about 25,000 students across Chile, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Mexico, and Peru. No further inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., grade level restrictions, item-completion thresholds, or missing-data rules) are provided in the text shown, so the analytic subsample definition cannot be extracted from the provided excerpt.

data.outcome_summary: This ICCS 2016 Latin American report focuses on students’ civic-related perceptions and attitudes, including views of public institutions and government, peaceful coexistence, and perceptions of social cohesion and diversity. It draws on the ICCS 2016 framework and combines the regional Latin American student questionnaire component with referencing to test, background, and contextual data from the international core instruments. The regional questionnaire was administered to approximately 25,000 students in five Latin American countries (Chile, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Mexico, and Peru), enabling both within-country comparisons and comparisons with ICCS 2009 for the four countries that participated in both cycles. The excerpt does not provide the technical details of scaling, benchmarks, or the specific statistical models used, and it does not report any machine-learning predictive performance metrics. Consequently, the methodological and benchmark interpretation should be taken from the ICCS 2016 technical report and the main ICCS 2016 international report.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The provided excerpt contains only bibliographic information, foreword, and a high-level description of the ICCS 2016 Latin American regional component. It does not include the methodological sections (sampling procedures, scaling, PVs, missing-data handling) nor any empirical predictive modeling results, so ML-specific fields (algorithms, metrics) and PV/missing-data handling cannot be extracted. This is therefore treated as a framework/report extraction with sparse methodological detail in the supplied text.
